Modified assessment using the FSR lens: Cautiously positive. The FOMC highlights strengthening activity and employment alongside continued, sizable accommodation (near‑zero policy rate and ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases) and an average‑inflation‑targeting framework that tolerates a temporary overshoot to re‑anchor expectations at 2 percent. The May 2021 Financial Stability Report, however, tempers this optimism: it notes elevated asset valuations and risk appetite, persistent funding‑market fragilities in parts of the nonbank sector, and still‑elevated business leverage, with pockets of stress in pandemic‑affected sectors such as commercial real estate. Offsetting these risks, banks remained well capitalized and household balance sheets were supported, contributing to resilience. Netting these FSR‑flagged vulnerabilities against the supportive policy backdrop and improving macro data, the tone remains positive but more guarded than a purely monetary‑policy read.
